speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to evaluate your complaint of progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin my assessment, can you tell me how long this has been occurring and if you notice any redness or warmth in the area? REQUEST TEST: CBC (Complete Blood Count).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal CBC results; since you are not showing signs of a systemic infection, are you currently unable to make a fist or extend the finger due to stiffness? REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CBC and ESR are normal, I suspect this is not an infectious process; can you describe if the swelling is pitting or if you have noticed any changes in the color or texture of the skin on that finger? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism of injury you described sounds like a significant crush or avulsion force. Given the location and your age, were you wearing a ring on that finger at the time of the injury? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion Injury of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus).

The mechanism of injury combined with the specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint while the finger remains extended is pathognomonic for a FDP tendon avulsion at the distal phalanx.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
